title: Supersede part of a record (narrow its scope) instead of all of it

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: ork's adj 168 (ui.structured-questions) changes two decided records, #104 (no structured answer options) and #109 (Enter submits, no confirm), only for structured questions; free-text answers keep #104 and #109. `adj supersede OLD --by NEW` replaces the whole record: OLD becomes superseded (internal/model/transition.go:75) and leaves `adj context`, which would drop the free-text rule. Today the only way is a full supersede plus restating the kept parts in NEW. ork's adj 169 (ui.sidebar-running against #82) has the same shape.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/supersede.go:27` (runSupersede): a narrowing form.
- `internal/model/transition.go:75` and `internal/model/record.go:364` (SupersededBy): a link that keeps OLD decided.
- `internal/cli/` context and show output: OLD shows "narrowed by NEW for SCOPE"; NEW lists OLD as narrowed.
- lint: both records stay decided; a narrowing link to a non-decided record is a problem.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Narrowing OLD by NEW keeps OLD decided and in `adj context`, with the scope note and NEW's ID.
- `adj show OLD` and `adj show NEW` print the link both ways; `adj lint` flags a narrowing link to an open or rejected record.
- A full supersede behaves as today.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Flag form to be decided in the slice (for example an in-part option with a scope text on supersede, or a separate narrows command). Keep the record format forward compatible (S46).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: go test ./...; go vet ./...; gofmt -l .; slicer check; adj lint.
